did_you_know.text: Did you know? Before going out to fight the Philistines, David inquired of the LORD and received instructions to go and save Keilah. When his men were afraid, he asked again and received further confirmation.
Did you know? Abiathar son of Ahimelech fled to David with the ephod in his possession. Through the ephod, David could inquire of the LORD and seek guidance in his affairs.
Did you know? After David learned that the people of Keilah might hand him over to Saul, he left the city with his men. At this point, his forces numbered about six hundred men.

Did you know? Although Saul hunted David constantly, the text emphasizes that the LORD did not deliver him into Saul’s hands. David moved among the wildernesses and strongholds, and in the Wilderness of Ziph he found refuge.

Did you know? Jonathan strengthened David not only with words of encouragement but also with an explicit promise: David would be king over Israel, and Jonathan would be his second-in-command. In this way, Jonathan showed his loyalty to David, even though Saul was his father.
Did you know? The people of Ziph gave Saul detailed information about David’s hiding place: the strongholds, the forest, and the hill of Hakilah, which is south of Jeshimon.

Did you know? When Saul had almost surrounded David in the Wilderness of Maon, a messenger arrived and reported a Philistine raid on the land. Saul had to stop pursuing David and go out to meet the Philistines; therefore, that place was called the Rock of Divisions.
Did you know? At the end of the chapter, David went up from there and settled in the strongholds of En Gedi, an area known for its cliffs and springs in the heart of the wilderness.
